subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class bounded memory write/CRUD contract in memory-core, and what limits, identity, duplicate/consolidation, snapshot, config, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: Source inspection shows the requested surface is missing, but implementing it would create public memory-write, config, persistence, and security behavior that needs maintainer direction.

options.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
options.body: Add a maintained add/list/replace/remove or unified memory tool with hard per-store limits, usage feedback, identity/selection, duplicate/consolidation, secret policy, docs, and tests.

options.title: Narrow to flush and diagnostics
options.body: Handle near-term memory bloat through existing memory-flush bounds, Control UI warnings, and curation work without exposing first-class CRUD yet.

options.title: Prototype externally first
options.body: Keep the core issue open while a plugin or operator facade proves the API shape before memory-core adopts it.

recommendation.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
recommendation.body: Add a maintained add/list/replace/remove or unified memory tool with hard per-store limits, usage feedback, identity/selection, duplicate/consolidation, secret policy, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The key unresolved choice is product/API direction across memory-core, config, persistence, and security, which fits the documented repository product owner role better than a single file owner.
